name: Behalf.bot - Parse YouTube
description: Turn any public YouTube URL into a timestamped transcript plus metadata. Resolves the video id from every URL shape, pulls manual or auto-generated captions through youtube-transcript-api with a configurable language fallback chain, and layers title, channel, duration, description and chapters on top via yt-dlp. Emits JSON for programmatic use, or timestamp-anchored markdown that drops straight into a draft. No API key needed for public videos.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false the skill does not trigger and setup.sh is not run.

default_language.description: Preferred caption language code tried first, e.g. 'en', 'pt', 'de'. Overridable per invocation with --lang. Consumed by the script as PARSE_YOUTUBE_DEFAULT_LANG.

fallback_languages.description: Caption languages appended after the preferred one, in order, when the preferred track does not exist. Set this to the languages the install actually reads. The default is English-only so the plugin makes no assumption about the operator's second language. Consumed as PARSE_YOUTUBE_FALLBACK_LANGS (comma-separated).

metadata.description: Fetch title, channel, duration, description and chapters via yt-dlp. Costs roughly 5 seconds per video. When false, or when yt-dlp is unavailable, those fields come back null and the transcript still works. Consumed as PARSE_YOUTUBE_METADATA.

metadata_timeout_seconds.description: Hard timeout on the yt-dlp metadata call. On expiry the metadata fields are null rather than the whole run failing. Consumed as PARSE_YOUTUBE_METADATA_TIMEOUT.

description_max_chars.description: How much of the video description to carry into the output. Descriptions are frequently link dumps, so the default truncates. Consumed as PARSE_YOUTUBE_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS.

activation._note: On-demand only. Invoked when the operator pastes a YouTube URL or asks for a transcript. Deliberately ships no message trigger: a bare YouTube link in a chat channel is far too common a thing to hijack, so dispatch stays model-driven.

system.name: python3
system.install: apt-get install python3 python3-pip (Debian) / your platform's package manager
system._explanation: The script is a single dependency-light Python file. Needs 3.10+ for the union type syntax it uses.

system.name: youtube-transcript-api
system._explanation: Pulls captions with no browser and no API key. Pinned to 1.2.4 because the 1.x API is instance-based (YouTubeTranscriptApi().list(video_id)) and yields FetchedTranscriptSnippet objects rather than dicts. A 0.x downgrade breaks the fetch path.

system.name: yt-dlp
system._explanation: Soft dependency, metadata only. YouTube changes its player often enough that yt-dlp ships near-weekly, so this is a floor rather than an exact pin - a stale yt-dlp fails against new videos. Missing or broken yt-dlp degrades to null metadata instead of failing the run.
